requested.title: Checkout action is referenced by a mutable major-version tag

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The complete DCO workflow currently references `actions/checkout@v5` at line 20, which is a mutable tag rather than an immutable commit object. The workflow runs for pull request events and invokes the third-party action before its own sign-off verification script, so a changed upstream `v5` tag would execute attacker-controlled code on the GitHub-hosted runner. The workflow-level `contents: read` permission gives the job a repository-scoped read token, and `persist-credentials: false` only prevents checkout from storing that credential in the local Git configuration; it does not prevent a malicious action from accessing the runtime token or checked-out source. The action could therefore read and exfiltrate repository contents and use its granted read API access, particularly impacting a private repository. No subsequent validation in the shell step constrains code already executed by the action, and the quoted environment-variable handling only mitigates shell injection in that later step. Git history shows the workflow was introduced using `actions/checkout@v5` and the later Dependabot change did not alter this reference, so the issue has not been fixed. This is an upstream-action supply-chain risk contingent on compromise or unauthorized mutation of the referenced action tag, but that is precisely what immutable SHA pinning is intended to eliminate.
